terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: By accessing or using GC Stats, you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service. Please read them carefully before using the platform.

service.title: About the Service
service.text: GC Stats is a community platform dedicated to archiving and sharing competitive data from Valorant Game Changers tournaments and related events. The service provides access to tournament results, player statistics, team information, and match data. GC Stats is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Riot Games.

access.title: Access & Eligibility
access.text: The platform is publicly accessible. Player profiles, team rosters, and match statistics are compiled by our team from publicly tracked tournament matches. Linking or editing a player profile, when applicable, is handled directly by our staff upon request and does not require authenticating a Riot account with GC Stats.

riotData.title: Riot Match Data
riotData.text: GC Stats retrieves match statistics directly from the official Riot Games API for matches identified as part of tracked tournaments. This data includes:
items: Riot IDs (game name and tagline) of participating players
Match history for matches identified as part of tracked tournaments
In-match statistics: scoreboard, performance summary, economy summary, and kill feed
riotData.optIn: Basic match participation (name, statistics) is recorded for any player appearing in a tracked tournament match, as this is public competitive data. Additional profile information (biography, socials, photo) is only added with the player's or team's consent.
riotData.correction: If you are a player appearing in this data and wish to request a correction or removal, you may contact us at any time (see our Privacy Policy for details).

prohibited.title: Prohibited Uses
prohibited.text: You agree not to use the platform or its API for any of the following purposes:
items: Gambling, betting, or any activity involving wagering on game outcomes
Spreading misinformation, fake statistics, or manipulated data
Harassing, targeting, or doxing players or community members
Any illegal activity under applicable law
Automated bulk scraping beyond normal API usage
Reselling or redistributing raw data as a standalone product

api.title: API Usage
api.text: GC Stats provides a public API for community and GC-related projects. Use of the API is subject to these Terms. The API is intended for informational, analytical, and community purposes. Rate limiting may be enforced. GC Stats reserves the right to revoke API access for any usage that violates these Terms or Riot Games's developer policies.

Team logos, player images, tournament assets, and any branding elements remain the property of their respective rights holders. GC Stats claims no ownership over game assets, which are the property of Riot Games.

Statistics displayed may contain errors; always verify with official sources for competitive decisions.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy informs you about how we handle data on this site, with a focus on transparency and respect for privacy.

analytics.title: Navigation & Statistics
analytics.text: We measure site audience in a completely anonymous way: these statistics never store an IP address, only the country, the page, and the time of visit, with no individual tracking or digital fingerprinting. If you create an account, your login session (IP address and user agent) is however stored temporarily for security purposes (protection against account takeover), as is standard for virtually every site with authentication.

publicData.title: Public Data
publicData.text: Profile information (handle, biography, social links, country) is voluntarily provided by the player and publicly displayed on the site. Match statistics are collected directly via the official Riot Games API for matches identified as part of tracked tournaments. All of this data is publicly accessible and shared through our API.

privateData.title: Private Data
privateData.text: The personal data we store is limited to what is needed to run the site and its account system: a Discord ID and a Riot ID to link a player profile, plus the account data described below for anyone who creates a user account.
privateData.discordUsage: Discord ID: Used to validate a player's identity when modifying their profile via our Discord.
privateData.riotUsage: Riot ID: Identified and assigned by our team from match data retrieved through the official Riot Games API. Used solely to associate match statistics with a player profile. Can be corrected or removed upon request.

accountData.title: User Account
accountData.text: Creating a user account (needed to react to news, manage a player profile, or administer the site) stores an email address, a password (hashed, never stored in plain text), your interface preferences, and, if you enable them, a two-factor authentication (2FA) secret, recovery codes, or passkeys. This information is never shared or made public.

socialLogin.title: Login via Discord, Twitter/X, or Twitch
socialLogin.text: You can link your account to Discord, Twitter/X, or Twitch to sign in faster. We then store your ID on that platform, your nickname, your avatar, and the access/refresh tokens needed to keep the connection alive (these tokens are only used to authenticate your account and are never shared). You can unlink these accounts at any time from your profile settings.
socialLogin.gravatar: Default avatar: If you don't have an avatar via a linked account, an image may be requested from Gravatar (Automattic) based on a hash of your email, a standard third-party service used by many websites.

moderation.title: Moderation & Community Safety
moderation.text: To keep the community safe, we keep a history of sanctions (warnings, bans) applied to an account or team, reports submitted by users (fraud, ban evasion, harassment, fake accounts, etc.), and an activity log of moderation actions.
moderation.retentionNote: To prevent ban evasion, a technical fingerprint (such as an email address) may be attached to a sanction and kept even after the associated account is deleted. The same applies to the report history and moderation log, which form a safety record kept independently of the account.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.subtitle: How GC Stats is developed, hosted and funded
transparency.intro: GC Stats is a non-profit, community-driven project. One of my goals was to build an ethical and transparent project, and that's exactly what this page is for: we reveal the source code, how we work, the finances, everything.

dev.title: Development
dev.body: The source code of GC Stats and all of our projects is open source and publicly available on GitHub. Anyone can review the code, report a bug or suggest an improvement.
dev.body2: Decisions about additions or new features on the site are made by the staff after discussion and a vote, taking community feedback into account. When in doubt about major decisions, polls are held on Discord or on Twitter.

hosting.title: Hosting & Infrastructure
hosting.body: We rely on a small set of providers to keep GC Stats fast, reliable and transparent. Here is exactly who hosts what, without ever reselling the data we collect.

cloudflareHosting.name: Cloudflare
cloudflareHosting.body: Hosts and deploys the GC Stats website on its Workers network: edge execution around the world, and a preview deployment for every change before it goes live.

cdn.name: Cloudflare
cdn.body: Caches our CSS/JS, as well as player, team & tournament images, on servers around the world to lighten the load on our own servers.

infomaniak.name: Infomaniak
infomaniak.role: Cloud, Public Cloud, mail & domain registrar
infomaniak.intro: Infomaniak, a Swiss provider, handles our cloud storage, our Public Cloud servers, our email, and our domain name registration.

cloud.title: Cloud
cloud.body: kDrive, Infomaniak's file storage service, used for our internal files and backups.

publicCloud.title: Public Cloud
publicCloud.body: Infomaniak servers that run our internal services and our database, connected privately to our Cloudflare infrastructure (Workers VPC).

database.title: Database
database.body: Hosted on our Public Cloud servers, it stores all of the site's data: players, teams, tournaments and matches.

mail.title: Email
mail.body: Handles the delivery and storage of all of our emails.

domain.title: Domain registrar
domain.body: Registers and manages our domain name (the name servers themselves are managed separately by Cloudflare).

quote.p1: Infomaniak is a Swiss provider that shares some of my values: privacy, the environment, and respect for its customers.
quote.p2: I already use kDrive, their VPS, and I used their NAS in the past. It mattered to me that Osthelia moved there too. I try to deploy as many services as possible with them, and even though it's slightly more expensive for some services, I think it's worth it.
quote.p3: I'm absolutely not paid to say this, if anything it's the opposite: our Drive and mail would be free with Google or Microsoft, while I pay €1.90 per user per month with Infomaniak.
quote.p4: I thought it was important to explain this choice, and especially to talk about Infomaniak: it's a lesser known provider, but one that deserves to be. Especially since a free mail account or a OneDrive subscription can be migrated to them without really paying more, for a service that's just as good, but with a minimum of respect for you, your privacy and our planet.

data.title: Data collected
data.body: We publicly document every piece of data we store: players, teams, tournaments and matches. No data is collected without a reason tied to the site's operation.

finance.title: Finance
finance.body: GC Stats publishes every single income and expense in a public ledger, updated with every movement.

openSource.title: Open source & contributions
openSource.body: We've decided to open source most of the project, to let the community help, we don't believe in closed source. All our repositories (except the admin dashboard) are open for contributions. Make sure to read our guidelines before submitting a Pull Request.

becomePublisher.title: Become a publisher
becomePublisher.intro: Already covering the Game Changers scene, or want to start? Publish your articles directly on GC-Stats.

what.title: What is a publisher?
what.body: A publisher is a media outlet (or an independent author) whose articles show up in GC-Stats' News section, with its own identity (logo, socials, dedicated page). We're not trying to replace you, just to give visibility to work we already think is worth showing.

freedom.title: Full editorial freedom
items: Your articles stay in their original language, we never translate on your behalf.
No minimum, no maximum: publish at your own pace.
We never write articles ourselves, the space is entirely yours, in your own style.

howTo.title: How to join
howTo.body: No self-service signup for now: reach out with your outlet's name (or your handle if publishing under your own name) and a few examples of your past work. We'll set up your access quickly.

supportUs.intro: GC-Stats isn't a standalone project: it's one of Osthelia's projects, the collective behind all of this. Here's who we are and where your support goes.

osthelia.body: Osthelia is fighting to build better alternatives in esports: free, accessible to everyone, easy to use, and built with communities rather than extracted from them.

descriptions.identity:
A person (player, coach, caster, observer, organizer...) only has one profile, even if their role changes over time. Teams and organizations have the right to edit/delete their "Additional information".

The Discord ID and Riot ID are never displayed or shared. They're provided by the person themselves via Discord, or identified by our team from match data.
descriptions.tournament: Every tournament has an identifier, a name, dates, a region, a category and a status. A tournament can be split into several stages (groups, playoffs...), themselves made of one or more containers (bracket or group). Teams register as "entrants", with a roster locked in for that specific tournament, separate from the team's permanent roster.
descriptions.matches:
We collect a lot of information about matches to provide detailed statistics. We gather:
- The basic match information (required)
- The match's vetoes
- The maps played, with the result and stats
- Aggregated stats per player and per map, what the site actually queries day to day

This data isn't always collected, but we try our best to obtain it in order to display the most complete stats possible.
descriptions.rawStats:
In addition to the aggregated stats above, we keep a round-by-round raw layer (kills, damages, economy, alive states) used to recompute those stats and to display round history.

Every player's position during key events (kill, plant, defuse) is kept in full detail indefinitely: it feeds our heatmaps and can't be reconstructed once aggregated.
descriptions.news:
Every news article has an identifier, a title, content and a status (draft, published, archived). An article can be linked to a team, a person or a tournament to appear on its profile.

The forum and emotes/reactions let the community interact with the site's content; messages hidden or removed by moderation stay tracked internally.
descriptions.account:
These tables only exist for people who created a user account (distinct from a person profile), required to react to news, manage a profile, or administrate the site.

Security data (password, 2FA, passkeys) is never shared. Linked Discord/Twitch accounts store an access token used only for authentication.

Moderation data (sanctions, anti-evasion fingerprints, reports, activity log) forms a security record kept independently of the account, even after its deletion, to prevent ban evasion.
descriptions.others:
We store the number of visits on each page per day; we don't store who viewed it or the exact time, only the approximate country/region.

This data is stored and private. It's never shared, we only use it to visualize site usage and adapt our infrastructure as needed.
